lead: Spotter stations: a picture, instrument, drug or test is shown; name it, say its use, how it is used and one complication or precaution.
f: Pinard fetal stethoscope (from 24 wk) · hand-held Doppler · tape for SFH · Cusco (bivalve, self-retaining) · Sims (needs an assistant: VVF, prolapse) · sponge-holding forceps · swabs · nitrazine paper
Amniotomy hook · cord clamp · episiotomy scissors · needle holder · delivery set · CTG machine · partogram sheet · newborn bag-valve-mask

Ventouse: Kiwi (hand pump), metal cups · forceps: Wrigley (outlet, CS), Neville-Barnes (low, mid), Kielland (rotation, sliding lock, little pelvic curve) · MVA syringe (60 mL) and Karman cannulae · curette, sound, Hegar dilators

sc: Forceps with a sliding lock and little pelvic curve → Kielland (rotational)

f: Foley catheter for induction · Bakri balloon (300–500 mL) and condom-catheter balloon for PPH tamponade · copper IUD (within 48 h or after 4 wk), implant, DMPA, combined pill

sc: Uterine balloon filled with 300–500 mL → Bakri balloon: PPH tamponade

f: Oxytocin (fridge) · ergometrine (dark, fridge; not in hypertension) · misoprostol 200 µg (no fridge) · carboprost · TXA · MgSO₄ 50% and calcium gluconate 10% · labetalol, hydralazine, nifedipine, methyldopa · aspirin · steroids · anti-D · iron · terbutaline · lidocaine · vitamin K

Urine dipstick · fern pattern: liquor · clot test: no clot at 7–10 min = DIC · CTG strip · scans: sac with yolk sac, CRL, snowstorm (mole), empty uterus with adnexal mass (ectopic) · lambda sign: dichorionic

tr: Always name the precaution with a drug
